narrative.thesis: Overall, biodiversity is driven by landscape heterogeneity: a stable rich core, consistently poorer edges, and sites whose value depends on the taxa considered. Maintaining habitat mosaics and structural complexity is key to long-term ecological resilience.
narrative.thesisSource: Every1Counts, 12-month analysis of Château Purcari, July 2026

dawnChorus.verdict: Rich chorus — the site is alive and little disturbed at dawn.
dawnChorus.text: At daybreak, birds sing all together: this is the dawn chorus. The richer it is in different species, the healthier the site. It is often the first indicator to drop when a habitat degrades — even before total richness changes.

narrative.refuge: Purcari stands out as the most species-rich site, highlighting its exceptional ecological quality and the diversity of habitats it offers, making it a particularly valuable refuge for bird biodiversity within the landscape.

protection.text: Not one hectare of this refuge holds any protected status.

terroir.line: Descifrând terroir-ul Purcari — de la sol la expresia vinului

narrative.nightMethod: civil twilight (sun < -6 deg) at the estate, per detection date

sites.label: Ridge core · east
sites.note: The only station that ran all 365 days. Anchor of both similarity clusters.

sites.label: Open farmland · west
sites.note: Poorest station on both methods, and the most daylight-bound: 89.7% of its animals move by day.

sites.label: Vineyard block · south
sites.note: Consistently intermediate. Lost to equipment failure after 01.11.25.

sites.label: Southern tip
sites.note: Low-diversity periphery. Its mammal community is 65% plant-eating — a grazing edge.

sites.label: Forest edge · east
sites.note: The starkest split on the estate: 2 species on camera, 123 in the air.

sites.label: Central grassland
sites.note: The richest and most stable acoustic station — the only site to hold its own statistical group.

sites.label: Northern woodland
sites.note: Loudest place on the estate — 7,859 bird detections — yet almost nothing walks past the camera.

sites.label: Western forest block
sites.note: Moved three times over the year. Strongest camera similarity pair on the estate.

sites.label: Interior forest
sites.note: Carries the heaviest mammals — the wild boar station.

sites.label: Northern woodland edge
sites.note: Highest camera richness on the estate: 18 species, 1,106 encounters.

sites.label: Southern margin
sites.note: Installed last, in January. The most nocturnal station: 56.8% of its life happens after dark.

sites.label: Château grounds
sites.note: One month of camera before the hardware moved to H9. Lightest, most aerial bird community on the estate.

species.note: Turtle dove — vulnerable, collapsing in Europe

species.name: Red-backed Shrike
species.note: Red-backed shrike — hedgerow specialist, Annex I
